learningObjective: Distinguish claims about FlashAttention that are algorithm-level truths from common overgeneralizations about performance.
stem: Select all statements about FlashAttention that are correct at the algorithm-and-analysis level (i.e., independent of any specific paper wall-clock number). (Choose all that apply.)

options.text: FlashAttention delivers a fixed wall-clock speedup (roughly 3-4x) uniformly across sequence lengths, batch sizes, and head dimensions on all modern GPUs, because it is designed to be independent of hardware configuration.

The backward pass of FlashAttention deliberately recomputes the softmax probabilities block-by-block from stored (m, l) statistics; this recomputation trades extra FLOPs for a much smaller HBM footprint.
FlashAttention is exact (bitwise up to summation-order rounding, not approximate) and does not change the FLOP count of forward attention.
FlashAttention's asymptotic HBM I/O scales as O(N^2 d / M), where M is on-chip memory per SM; the gap versus O(N^2) baselines grows with N.

explanation: Options B, C, D are correct; option A is incorrect. A (Wrong): benchmark_leak — a specific measurement is treated as a universal fact. B (Correct): backward design. C (Correct): exactness and preserved FLOP count. D (Correct): paper's IO complexity result. General context: Speedup depends strongly on N, d, batch, and hardware SMEM.

optionExplanations.C: Correct: exactness and preserved FLOP count.

assumptions: 'FlashAttention' refers to the FA v1/v2 exact algorithms.
'Wall-clock speedup' is shape and hardware dependent.
nonImplications: Does not imply FA is beneficial on all attention shapes; very small N may not benefit.
Does not imply FA is the endpoint of attention optimization; ring/tree/sparse variants extend it.
